Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle. Ishan Kishan and Shubman Gill are the two openers for India while West Indies are going with spin straightaway as Akeal Hosein has the new ball in hand. Here wr go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, West Indies have posted a decent total but their bowlers will need to be in point to defend this against a strong batting line-up of the visitors. India will be confident enough of getting to this total as their batters are in good form and will look to take the first game of the series. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

India, on the other hand, were hot and cold with their bowling effort, but ultimately will be happy with how things went. They leaked a few too many boundaries at the start but Yuzvendra Chahal turned the game around by getting rid of King and Mayers in the same over which was followed by Kuldeep Yadav as he dismissed Charles soon after. They were taken aback by the clean hitting of Pooran and Powell but still managed to squeeze in some good overs. Hardik Pandya brought himself back in the attack and got the big wicket of Pooran which has made a significant difference in the total. The return of Kul-Cha proved to be the right decision for the visitors while Arshdeep Singh also picked up a couple of wickets in the end and Mukesh Kumar also bowled a brilliant last over. All in all a complete bowling performance from them.

West Indies got off to a brisk start with Brandon King finding the boundaries with ease but Kyle Mayers struggled to even get off the mark. They suffered a setback when both their openers were sent back in the same over while Johnson Charles also couldn't do much. After that, Nicholas Pooran joined his skipper Rovman Powell at the crease and started to counter-attack and took the Indian bowlers to the cleaners. Unfortunately, Pooran holed out at 41 but Powell continued to take on the bowlers along with Shimron Hetmyer but they kept losing wickets which took the momentum away from them as they were restricted under 150 with Powell top scoring with 48 off 32 balls.

A fine bowling effort from India! They have restricted the host to 149 runs and never let them settle in. There were moments of individual brilliance for the Windies but once again they failed to perform collectively. Hardik Pandya managed his bowlers really well and with some excellent death bowling, they will be the happier side going into the break.

Another appeal, and given. King goes for the review, UltraEdge shows no bat involved and Ball Tracking indicates three reds. West Indies two down now!

There is an appeal for LBW, and up goes the finger. However, looking at the replay it seems it may have missed the off pole, but Mayers walked back anyway. West Indies lose their first wicket!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the prematch formalities as the umpires walk towards the pitch. The Indian players are in a huddle on the ground for a few last-minute instructions from Hardik Pandya before taking their respective positions on the field. Brandon King and Kyle Mayers will open the inning for West Indies and will want to get a good partnership going here. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball in his hand and will begin proceedings. Let's play...

We are close to the start of the game but first, the two sets of players and the match officials line up for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Trinidad and Tobago first, followed by India's national anthem and finally the national anthem of West Indies.

Hardik Pandya, the skipper of India says that the whole plan for the tour is to try out their bench strength and they may need to come back here soon for the World Cup. Adds that it is all about the preparations and giving players an opportunity to prove themselves before the 50-over World Cup later this year. Claims that he tries to keep things simple as it is about improving and showing progress. Mentions that he does not worry much about the mistakes but concentrates on the process. Informs that Umran Malik and Ravi Bishnoi miss out as they have gone with three spin bowlers.

Rovman Powell says that they will bat first. Adds that India have a lot of spinners so they will look to put up a big total on the board. Shares that the visitors are a very good side. Mentions that running between the wickets is very important and it is not all about scoring boundaries. Informs they are playing six batters and two all-rounders in Jason Holder and Romario Shepherd.

India (Playing XI) - Shubman Gill, Ishan Kishan (WK), Suryakumar Yadav, Tilak Varma (on debut), Hardik Pandya (C), Sanju Samson, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Yuzvendra Chahal, Arshdeep Singh, Mukesh Kumar (on T20I debut).

West Indies (Playing XI) - Kyle Mayers, Brandon King, Johnson Charles (WK), Nicholas Pooran, Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell (C), Romario Shepherd, Jason Holder, Akeal Hosein, Obed McCoy, Alzarri Joseph.
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favour of the West Indies. They have elected to BAT first.
Live pictures show Tilak Varma receiving his India cap as he makes his international bow. Meanwhile, Mukesh Kumar will also make his T20I debut to represent India in all three formats.

India, on the other hand, will be riding high on confidence as they gear up for their 200th T20I. Only Pakistan have achieved this feat so far. They have rested the likes of Kohli, Rohit and Jadeja but their youngsters took the opportunity and registered a big win in the final ODI without them and will look to do something similar here. Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan makes up a powerful opening duo but that could change as in-form Yashasvi Jaiswal could make his debut. They have the current World No. 1 batter in Sky who has the ability to score all around the park. Hardik Pandya will be leading the side again and he will have Arshdeep Singh as his lead pacer in this format while Avesh Khan is also back in the squad. Mukesh Kumar has impressed on this tour and could play a part while Umran Malik can be given more game time as well. They have variety of spin options as well and it will be interesting to see the combination and also if Yuzvendra Chahal gets a chance after sitting out in the ODIs. Will they continue the winning momentum and get the victory? Or will the Windies take a 1-0 in the series? We will find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

West Indies have named a strong squad and have recalled the likes of Oshane Thomas and Shimron Hetmyer to boost their team even more. Unlike the longer formats, their players can express themselves better here. Johnson Charles made his return to the national team last year after a long gap and has performed well in thia format while Brandon King has also scored runs at the top but needs to improve his strike rate. Nicholas Pooran is in his prime form while Kyle Mayers, Hettie and Rovman Powell are going to be crucial too. Alzarri Joseph and Akeal Hosein will be the key bowlers for them. Most of their players have played in the Indian T20 League and can use that experience against the visitors to get the better of them but they know it is going to be a difficult task. The hosts could take inspiration from their last T20I series where they defeated a strong South African side. They need their senior players to step up and start the series on a positive note.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! We are all set for the first T20I of this five-match series between West Indies and India. These two teams battled it out in the longer formats before this where the visitors reigned supreme, but the hosts are better suited to this format and will provide a tougher challenge. Windies have a good chance of winning this T20I series and end their draught since 2017 against India while the Men in Blue will look to win all the formats on this tour.
... MATCH DAY ...

India took home the Test series and now they have also won the ODIs, after winning the decider with a thumping performance. This long tour moves to its final phase where we will see both teams have a go at each other in the shortest format as they gear up for a five-match T20I series. The first game will be played at the Brian Lara Stadium in Trinidad and Tobago. West Indies are known for this format but their record against the visitors is not very encouraging as they have lost 10 out of their last 11 games. They will hope to change their fortunes and give their fans something to cheer for, while India will want to continue their dominance. The hosts will count on Brandon King and Kyle Mayers as the two openers and they have scored good runs as well but their strike rate isn't that good, so they could think about getting Johnson Charles in the team. Nicholas Pooran has been their leading scorer since last year and can float through the batting order depending on the situation. He recently helped New York win the USA T20 League with a blistering 137 off just 55 balls and will be high on confidence. Their skipper, Rovman Powell is also having a good time in T20Is and will also have the backing of Shimron Hetmyer and Jason Holder in the middle order. Alzarri Joseph will once again be the key bowler for them and he also took a five-for in the series against South Africa earlier this year. Akeal Hosein will act as the main spinner and has the experience of playing in different conditions which will be a big help. Romario Shepherd and Roston Chase will look to provide the required support. Holder can also bowl some crucial overs in the middle while they also have Obed McCoy and Oshane Thomas to try different bowling combinations. They will hope to bounce back from the ODI series defeat and start this one on a positive note. India, on the other hand, have a pretty young squad and this is good for the players to get some international exposure. Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan will likely open for them with the latter coming off three half-centuries in the longer format while Gill struggled a bit but managed to play a good knock in the last game. The opening duo could change if they decided to put Yashasvi Jaiswal into the mix who had a brilliant debut Test scoring a double hundred. However, we all saw what Gill can do in the Indian T20 League and if he gets into his groove, no bowler is safe. Tilak Varma could also make his debut in this series after his consistent performance in recent times. Suryakumar Yadav will look to add to his tally of runs as he is one of the best batters in this format across the globe. Hardik Pandya will be leading the side and will be crucial with both bat and ball. He will also have Sanju Samson and Axar Patel which make up a strong middle order. Arshdeep Singh will be the frontline pacer for them, along with Umran Malik, and Mukesh Kumar who is having a good tour. However, it will be interesting to see which spinners will play as India seem to be experimenting a lot. They have Yuzvendra Chahal, Kuldeep Yadav, and Ravi Bishnoi, and we could once again see Kul-Cha playing together. Even though they have rested the senior players, they still have the quality to challenge any opposition. Let's find out which team takes the lead in this series.
